name: Planche Lean
summary: An isometric calisthenics hold in a plank position with the shoulders leaned forward past the wrists to develop straight-arm pushing strength and scapular protraction.

setup: Place your hands on the floor roughly shoulder-width apart, with fingers spread and pointed slightly outward to relieve wrist pressure.
Step your feet back into a push-up plank position with feet together and toes pointed into the ground.
Lock your elbows completely straight and actively push the floor away to achieve maximum scapular protraction and depression.
Tuck your pelvis into a posterior pelvic tilt, bracing the abs and squeezing the glutes to form a solid hollow body.
steps: Keeping the arms fully locked and core tight, shift your body weight forward by leaning your shoulders ahead of your wrists.
Hold the maximum forward lean you can sustain with completely straight elbows, protracted shoulder blades, and a flat lower back.
Maintain the static hold for the prescribed duration.
Carefully shift your weight backward to exit the hold and rest on your knees.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously with shallow, controlled breaths while maintaining rigid abdominal and chest tension throughout the hold.
cues: Push the floor away to round the upper back.
Tuck the tailbone and squeeze the glutes.
Lean forward onto the tips of the toes.

common_faults.fault: Bending the elbows as the forward lean increases.
common_faults.correction: Fully lock the arms and rotate the elbow pits forward; decrease the forward lean angle until the elbows can stay rigidly straight.

common_faults.fault: Losing scapular protraction and allowing the chest to sink between the shoulder blades.
common_faults.correction: Actively spread the shoulder blades apart and push the ground away throughout the entire duration.

common_faults.fault: Sagging at the hips or hyper-extending the lumbar spine.
common_faults.correction: Squeeze the glutes hard and pull the ribcage down toward the pelvis into a hollow-body position.

precautions: Thoroughly warm up the wrists, shoulders, and biceps tendons before performing intense straight-arm leans.
If wrist mobility limits your lean angle or causes pain, perform the exercise using parallettes or turn the hands outward.
